# decock-2026-forum-interstitiale-working-paper
- **URL:** https://zenodo.org/records/21633712 (concept DOI; resolves to latest version, record 22011267; abstract read via a reader proxy + Zenodo API https://zenodo.org/api/records/22011267 and /versions; 40-page v3 PDF downloaded from the API file endpoint and text-extracted locally) · also https://foruminternum.org/ , /brief , /resources (via a reader proxy) · **Accessed:** 2026-09-16 · **For:** v2→v3 response round, slice M (M3)
- **Citation (her own suggested form, foruminternum.org/resources):** "Caroline De Cock, Protecting the Thinking Process in Human-AI Interaction: The Forum Interstitiale Between Thought and Expression (working paper, July 2026), https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21633712". Zenodo: resource type Preprint; author affiliation "information labs"; **v1 published 2026-07-27** (doi 10.5281/zenodo.21633713; file "…27072026 v2.1.pdf"), **v2 2026-08-03** (10.5281/zenodo.21769629), **v3 2026-08-19** (10.5281/zenodo.22011267; file "…-190826.pdf"). Zenodo labels the latest "Version v3"; the PDF title page still says "July 2026." Not peer reviewed.
- **What it establishes:** De Cock published the "line drawn when thinking left no trace" diagnosis on 27 July 2026, before the essay. Wording differs by version — quote with the version. She proposes a third, *qualified* zone; explicitly "only works upwards"/no-demotion; and she already frames her proposal as the answer to (i) Bublitz's dilution objection and (ii) McCarthy-Jones & Walmsley's conditional absoluteness. She also already cites Pin (2026), Ligthart (2025), Richards, Penney, Clark & Chalmers, Hutchins — i.e., most of the essay's §III apparatus.
- **Key passages:**
  - Abstract, **v1 (27 July 2026) and v2**: "Doctrine calls the two sides of that line the forum internum and the forum externum. The line was drawn when thinking left no trace. It no longer holds." **v3 (19 Aug 2026; also PDF p. 1)**: "However, the line was drawn when thinking left no trace, and with current technological developments, it no longer holds." → The review's clause "the line was drawn when thinking left no trace" is verbatim in all versions; as a free-standing *sentence* it is v1/v2 only.
  - Abstract (all versions; v3 adds "it claims"): "courts refuse protection because the machine is not a professional, like a doctor or a lawyer, and industry asks for a new privilege because it claims it behaves like one. Both assume that protection depends on what the machine is. This article argues that it depends on what the person is doing."
  - Abstract: "It proposes the forum interstitiale, a third zone between the two classical fora, protecting the thinking process under a standard stronger than ordinary expression law but short of absolute." (Paper says "third zone"/"third category"; the *website* says "third space" and "third room": "Between the room where you think alone and the square where you speak, there is a third room.")
  - Abstract v3: "The interstitial zone the article proposes only works upwards. It raises acts the current binary approach abandons and takes nothing from the absolute core, which answers the objection that widening protection dilutes it." (v1: "The zone only works upwards.") Website: "The forum interstitiale only works upwards. It lifts the anteroom out of the unprotected class it currently falls into. It takes nothing away from the absolute core, and nothing the law already protects can be pulled down into it."
  - "heightened, not absolute" is the **website's** phrase ("Give that space a name and a standard of its own, heightened, not absolute…"); the paper's is "heightened but qualified protection" (PDF p. 4, p. 32).
  - PDF p. 4: "Any cognitive act that leaves the skull falls, by default, into the outer category or out of the framework entirely, into the residual class of business records held by a third party."
  - PDF pp. 4–5: "First, the forum interstitiale is qualified, deliberately, rather than absolute. The most forceful objection to expanding freedom of thought, pressed by Jan Christoph Bublitz among others, is that widening the absolutely protected sphere dilutes and jeopardizes the absoluteness of its core. The interstitial zone concedes the point rather than fighting it". (fn 7 cites Bublitz 2014 ARSP and Ligthart et al., "Rethinking the Right to Freedom of Thought," 22 HRLR ngac028 (2022).)
  - PDF p. 7 (the unobservability premise): "The architecture of the forum internum rested, from the beginning, on a factual premise as much as a normative one. Blackstone wrote that no temporal tribunal 'can search the heart, or fathom the intentions of the mind' … The forum internum was absolute partly because it was thought unreachable, protected, in effect, by its own opacity. It was considered a black box."
  - PDF p. 8 (on McCarthy-Jones & Walmsley): "My article departs from McCarthy-Jones and Walmsley on the protection standard. Their proposal extends absolute protection into the forum externum, conditioned on the purposes of self-government and truth-seeking. … a proposal that extends absoluteness must still defend the absoluteness of what it has extended. The forum interstitiale reaches the same acts through a qualified tier, and therefore does not have to."
  - PDF p. 9: "Bublitz and co-authors have warned that the manifested vs unmanifested distinction is vulnerable to critique from extended cognition, while insisting that the response cannot be an indefinite expansion of the absolute sphere, because a right that covers everything absolutely will end up protecting nothing absolutely. This is the dilution objection, and it is the strongest argument in the field against protecting external cognitive acts as thought." (fn 20 → Ligthart et al. 2022. NB: this is De Cock's paraphrase; Ligthart et al. 2022 not opened this round.)
  - PDF pp. 32–33, five elements: predictability; heightened access threshold ("individualized suspicion and a demonstrated need"; class access "presumptively impermissible"); structural safeguards; protection against pre-emptive restriction (+ notice); "Fifth, the no-demotion rule. The interstitial zone only works upwards."
  - PDF p. 34 (§VI.C): "A right that absolutely protects everything functionally connected to cognition would collapse at first contact with a compelling countervailing interest … The dilution objection does not defeat this proposal. It explains why the middle tier must exist, and why it must be qualified."
- **Reliability:** Primary for De Cock's position; self-published preprint by an EU digital-policy practitioner/advocate; not peer reviewed; versions changed wording within three weeks.
- **Relevance to this project:** §III. The review is right that De Cock has priority on the diagnosis and on "what the person is doing." More than that: her qualified-tier architecture is very close to what the essay's "rationale, not its unlimited scope" sentence gestures at, and she has already stated *what* the standard contains (five elements). The essay must cite her and say what differs (if anything: e.g., the essay's grounding in the forum internum's rationale vs. her stand-alone third forum; her no-demotion rule is something the essay could adopt). Supersedes the "working paper not opened" line in decock-forum-interstitiale.md.
